decisions: THE MODAL'S GREYED ROW IS A COURTESY; THE SERVER ACTION IS THE GUARD. assignDriver had NO availability check at all - a stale tab, a second window or a direct action call went straight through to the write. The rule now lives in lib/driver-assignment.ts and BOTH the Fleet modal and the server action call the same driverAvailability(). Same shape as the payslip hire-date gate: the friendly sentence is the normal path, the refusal before the write is the enforcement.

THE FIX WAS NOT A SECOND COPY OF THE RULE IN THE ACTION. Writing the availability check inline in assignDriver would have recreated exactly the drift that three migrations were just spent removing from truck status. One expression, two callers, neither able to hold a private opinion.

DRIVER STATE IS NOT AN AVAILABILITY MODEL. v_driver_state_now / lib/driver-state.ts must NOT gate assignment: off_duty means 'has no truck', so every genuinely assignable driver in the picker is off_duty and a gate reading state != off_duty would refuse every legitimate assignment on the page. The on-leave FACT is still shared - both paths resolve through lib/leave's periodCoversToday - so there is one date rule, not one rule and one view of it.

WHAT BLOCKS AN ASSIGNMENT, ENUMERATED: terminated (invisible in the UI because the picker's fetch filters it - a FILTER IS NOT A GATE, so only a direct call reaches it), assigned to another non-terminated truck, and on leave today. What deliberately does NOT block: drivers.status, drivers.active, a truck in maintenance, or a driver holding in-flight trips.

THE CURRENT DRIVER IS EXEMPT, AND THE LABEL IS NOT. Re-selecting the driver already on this truck is a no-op and must not start erroring the day they go on leave. But the modal still reads 'On leave today' beside that clickable row, because both statements are true; collapsing label into blockedReason would have to lie about one of them.

THE GATE FAILS CLOSED. If any of the four availability reads errors, the assign is refused rather than allowed - an unreadable availability fact is not an available driver. Same reasoning 0114 put into SQL, applied here in TypeScript.

freeDriverFromOtherTrucks IS NO LONGER CALLED BY assignDriver. It let an assign steal a driver off another truck without tripping 0002's partial unique index, but the modal has always locked that case and the gate now refuses it - so leaving the call would make the action quietly capable of a move the UI forbids. The helper stays for createTruck, which legitimately needs it. The unique index remains the backstop for the read-then-write race and 23505 is translated into a sentence rather than shown raw.

THE GATE USES todayKey(), THE SAME LOCAL CLOCK app/fleet/page.tsx USES. A UTC date here would disagree with the modal for the three hours after midnight Riyadh - the exact bug class just fixed on this page's 30-day window.

create-or-replace CANNOT REMOVE A COLUMN EITHER. CLAUDE.md section 6 records the append-only lock for adding one; the same restriction forbids dropping one, so 0120 has to be a DROP + CREATE. That is safe only because nothing depends on the view - verified three ways (dependent views, functions, pg_depend rewrite entries: all zero).

A REVOKE DOES NOT SURVIVE A DROP. Supabase's pg_default_acl grants anon on every newly created relation in public, so a plain drop-and-create silently hands anon SELECT back and reverts the view to owner-run. In 0120 the security footer is enforcement, not restatement.

No driver column was ever written. FOUR THINGS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. (1) tests/driver-assign-gate.spec.ts needs NO diagnostic route and NO auth bypass, so unlike the older suites it does not rot at teardown - it drives the pure rule, which IS the whole decision. What it cannot cover is the server action's four reads: without a session RLS returns zero rows, the gate would refuse for the WRONG reason, and the test would still go green. That half was proven against real rows through the MCP. (2) A FILTER IS NOT A GATE. Terminated drivers never appear in the picker, which is why nobody noticed the action would happily assign one. Any 'the UI does not offer it' argument is an argument about reachability, not about enforcement. (3) THE DASHBOARD'S TRUCK COUNTS NOW COME FROM lib/actions/truck-state.ts, NOT v_fleet_state_now. After 0120 the view has no truck columns at all. A wrong truck count is a bug in lib/truck-status.ts or its fetcher - do not re-add the view's derivation to 'fix' one. (4) BUILD ONLY VIA ./scripts/safe-build.sh. It exits non-zero if dev is live - it fired correctly this batch, so the build ran with --dist-dir .next-verify and dev on port 3002 was left untouched. next build also REWRITES tsconfig.json, so git checkout -- tsconfig.json afterwards.
